newsitem.title: FRANCE: Germany says private firms key to defence shakeout.
newsitem.headline: Germany says private firms key to defence shakeout.

text.p: Germany's defence minister on Friday said Europe's industrial consolidation depended on strong private sector companies -- to respond to competition from the United States.
"If we want to create strong companies in the face of American competition in Europe, they need to be private companies," Volker Ruhe told reporters at the Paris air show.
Ruhe was speaking on the eve of a keynote speech to be given by French Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin here on Saturday.
Industry executives are eager to hear the government's policy on Thomson-CSF and Aerospatiale, both earmarked for privatisation by the previous conservative government.

Ruhe had earlier visited the air show pavilion of private French group Lagardere, whose Matra division and its British partners are forming a missiles and space joint venture with Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa).

Lagardere's MMS satellite joint venture with GEC and its Matra BAe Dynamics tie-up with British Aerospace Plc successfully courted Dasa away from its long-standing French partner Aerospatiale, despite years of negotiations between state-owned Aerospatiale and Dasa.

"To build a European defence industry capable of standing up to global competition and which can rival the United States, I believe that we have to really build European companies and support them," Ruhe said.
"We have to look at setting up strong private companies in this area," he said.
Ruhe was giving a news conference with his French counterpart, Alain Richard, on the signing of contracts to set up production lines for the Franco-German Tiger combat helicopter.

Richard, appointed in France's new Socialist-led government nearly three weeks ago, said that Europe had won markets using different structures from the competition in the past -- the challenge now was to find different competitive solutions.
Richard declined to go into further details on the new govenment's defence policy ahead of Jospin's air show speech.
Jospin spoke of broad consolidation but also gave little away on defence in a policy speech to parliament on Thursday.
"Our (defence) enterprises must consolidate, to restore and increase their competitiveness so they can fully participate in future cooperation projects in Europe," he said.

"Europe is important for our defence. The government hopes to instill a new dynamism in the cooperation that will develop in this area. It is thus urgent to adopt a new and more coherent policy for the defence industries," he said.

The previous conservative government had planned to merge Aerospatiale with combat plane maker Dassault Aviation and privatise the new group. It had also launched the sale of the state's 58 percent stake in electronics firm Thomson-CSF.
The Socialist election campaign was hostile to privatisations, with some party officials favouring the creation of a large defence group made up of Aerospatiale, Thomson-CSF and Dassault Aviation.
Lagardere had bid against telecommunications giant Alcatel Alsthom in the Thomson-CSF sell-off.
